searchedFor: glob packages/cli/test/** for a command/e2e-level suite
findings.summary: The `output` "regression guard for #660" cannot fail on the regression it claims to guard
findings.evidence: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:157-164 comments itself as "Regression guard for #660" and asserts `output({a:1},'json')` prints the body. But the actual regression this PR fixes lives at the ~30 call sites that used to pass `opts.quiet` (e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:83, cells.ts:26). After the signature change, `output` unconditionally prints regardless of quiet, so the assertion holds trivially and would ALSO have held on the old code (which was called with quiet=false in this test's shape). If someone reintroduced suppression at a call site (`if (!opts.quiet) output(...)`) or re-added a defaulted `quiet` param, this test still passes. Nothing in packages/cli/test parses `--quiet` through a command action and asserts the body is still written to stdout — namespaces.test.ts:11 shows the createProgram()-based harness exists to do exactly that but only inspects option metadata. The comment's fallback claim ("a caller that tries to pass one fails to compile") is a type-level assertion never exercised by any test (no expectTypeError / ts-expect-error case).

findings.summary: Deleted quiet test for `outputError` replaced by an unrelated case; the new "errors print even under quiet" contract is untested
findings.evidence: The diff removes `it('honors quiet by exiting 1 without emitting stderr')` and substitutes `it('stringifies non-Error throwables')` (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:137-141), which exercises the pre-existing `String(error)` branch, not the changed behavior. The new documented contract in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:44-51 — that the error envelope survives `--quiet` — has no test at any level: every remaining outputError test calls it directly with no quiet notion, and no command-level test runs a failing command with `--quiet` to assert stderr is non-empty and exitCode is 1. Net effect: a behavior change (quiet no longer silences errors) shipped with strictly less coverage of quiet than before.

findings.summary: Production entrypoint uses `program.parse()` (sync) with async action handlers, so the behavior the new `--quiet` guard asserts via `parseAsync` is not what ships
findings.evidence: `bin.ts:27` calls `program.parse()`, but every registered action is `async function (...)` (e.g. `docs.ts:70`, `cells.ts:16`). Commander only awaits action promises in `parseAsync`; with `parse()` the returned promise is dropped. The new regression guard (`test/output.test.ts:240`) drives `parseAsync`, so it proves the body/error-envelope behavior only for a path the binary never takes. Any action rejection becomes an unhandled rejection (raw Node stack, no `{error:{code,message}}` envelope, exit code not the one `outputError` set), and nothing keeps the process alive until the async action completes. `parseAsync().catch(outputError)` would make the guard faithful.

searchedFor: read cells.ts, sheets-import.ts, docs.ts action bodies for code outside try
findings.summary: `sheets cells batch` parses JSON outside its try/catch, so malformed input escapes the error-envelope path entirely
findings.evidence: `cells.ts:110-120` runs `JSON.parse(dataStr)` and the stdin read/`JSON.parse` before the `try` that starts at line 132. A bad `--data '{'` (or a stdin read error) throws inside the async action, bypassing `outputError`, so no `{error:{code:'ERROR',message:...}}` reaches stderr and `process.exitCode = 1` is never set. Combined with `bin.ts:27`'s `program.parse()` (no `parseAsync`, no `.catch`), it surfaces as an unhandled-rejection trace — exactly the invariant the delta's new test ('prints the error envelope on stderr and exits 1') claims to protect, on a command the guard does not cover.

findings.summary: `bin entrypoint` tests assert on source text, not behavior; one assertion is vacuous
findings.evidence: The `bin entrypoint` describe (test/output.test.ts:303-318) `readFileSync`s src/bin.ts and string-matches it. `expect(source).toContain('outputError')` is satisfied by the import on bin.ts:13 (and by the word inside the comment on bin.ts:33) regardless of whether the catch handler calls it — it passes even if the catch body were `{}`. `expect(source).toMatch(/\.catch\(/)` matches any `.catch(` anywhere in the file, on any promise. Likewise `toContain('program.parseAsync(')` / `not.toMatch(/program\.parse\s*\(/)` pass for aliased calls (`const p = program; p.parse()`) or a `parseAsync(...)` whose promise is never awaited/handled. The claimed behavior — a rejection escaping an action handler is turned into the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope with exit 1 — is never executed, so these two tests are presented as coverage of bin.ts but cannot fail if that behavior breaks.

searchedFor: grep for parseAsync/spawn in test dir via output.test.ts inspection
findings.summary: No behavioral test for the new `parseAsync().catch(outputError)` entrypoint path
findings.evidence: bin.ts:35-37 is the new behavior (unhandled action rejection → error envelope + exitCode 1). The only test touching it is the source-string describe at test/output.test.ts:303. I searched packages/cli/test for any import or execution of bin.ts (grep for 'bin', 'parseAsync', 'spawn', 'execFile' across packages/cli/test) and found only the readFileSync source check; no test registers a command whose action rejects outside its own try/catch and asserts the envelope/exit code. A test could register a throwing action on a program and await `parseAsync().catch(outputError)`-equivalent wiring, or exercise a real command whose failure path escapes the handler (e.g. getConfig/getClient throwing before the try).
